intro: Word for compliance officers on Mac covers four jobs: drafting policies, comparing versions, tracking edits and approvals, and keeping a version log. Use Review > Compare > Compare Documents to check two files, and a review history table to record who changed what. The rest of this page shows each job in Word for Mac, the bugs to check, and where Lazur helps.

Build one policy template with a title page, a version field and a review history table before you write.

blocks.text: Most compliance work in Word is less about writing and more about tracking. A reviewer rewrites a clause, someone asks what changed, and you need the answer in minutes. Word on Mac can give you that answer, but only if you set it up before the first draft goes out.
Why compliance officers still work in Word on Mac

Policies, procedures, codes of conduct and investigation templates usually start life as Word files. Many teams move them into a document system later, and many never do. The 2025 Healthcare Compliance Benchmark found that half of compliance offices manage compliance documents manually. Word is often where that manual work happens.

Time is the bigger cost. Hyperproof's 2026 IT Risk and Compliance Benchmark found that 76% of respondents spend 30% or more of their time on repetitive administrative tasks. Bright Defense, which summarizes the same figure, reports that integrated, automated programs spend 33% of team time on that work. Ad hoc programs spend 39%. Better tools help, but your habits in Word matter just as much.

Most of your Word time falls into four jobs. You draft or update a policy. You compare two versions. You track edits and approvals. You keep a log of what changed. The sections below take them in that order, with the menu paths and the traps that cost people time.
Set up one policy template before you write

Start from a template, not a blank page. A template fixes the layout, so every reviewer reads the same structure. Collaboris publishes a free Word policy template built this way. It has a title page with a version number, a table of contents, and nine sections.

The nine sections run from introduction, purpose and scope, and definitions through a flow chart, policy details, related policies, policy owner, appeals, and review history. Copy the template for your company. Keep the title page, the version field and the review history. Delete the sections you do not use, but keep the review history. It is the record of who changed the policy and why.

blocks.text: Collaboris recommends keeping superseded versions, not only the current one. It says the review history table and your SharePoint version history together give the record. It also cites the HIPAA Security Rule for keeping written policies for six years. Confirm which rule applies to your business before you set a retention period.

Use real heading styles so the table of contents builds itself. Select a section title and press ⌘⌥1 for Heading 1. Use ⌘⌥2 for Heading 2 on subsections. Insert the table of contents from the References tab, then update it after each review. Step-by-step guides are at /how-to/apply-heading-styles-in-word and /how-to/insert-a-table-of-contents-in-word.
Compare two versions with Compare Documents

This is the job you will do most. A reviewer sends back a changed file, and you need to see every change before you approve it. Compare Documents in Word for Mac does that. It shows the differences as revision marks in a new document.

items: Open the newer version in Word for Mac.
Go to Review > Compare > Compare Documents.
Select the original file, then the revised file.
Click OK. Word creates a new document with revision marks.
Read the new document. Your two source files stay unchanged.

blocks.text: Microsoft's guide for this feature was written for Word 2019 for Mac. Newer menus may look slightly different, so trust the labels on your screen. The steps match in principle. Our walkthrough is at /how-to/compare-two-documents-in-word.

blocks.title: Grayed-out files on 16.109
blocks.text: On Word for Mac version 16.109, files can look grayed out in the Compare file picker, so you cannot select them. Click Show Options, then change the file type from Templates to All Files. Microsoft last updated this article on May 18, 2026.

blocks.title: Desktop only
blocks.text: Compare and Merge is desktop only. Microsoft's features comparison lists it as unavailable in Word for the web. If a reviewer edits online, download the file and compare it in Word for Mac.
Edge cases that catch people

items: Comparing against the wrong version. A draft compared with an older draft shows old edits as new. Compare against the last approved final.
Assuming compare shows authorship. It shows what differs between two files. It does not prove who made each change.
Ignoring comments. Old comments can clutter the result. Read the comments pane before you sign off.
Editing the source file during the review. Work on the compared copy so the baseline stays the same.

blocks.text: Track edits and approvals without losing the record

Track Changes turns every edit into a visible mark. Turn it on before a reviewer starts. In Word for Mac, press ⌘⇧E, or go to Review > Track Changes. Microsoft's comparison page lists Track Changes in both the desktop and web versions of Word.

Track Changes is not an approval system. The Collaboris template has no acknowledgment or approval section. It points to a separate acknowledgment form and an Excel acknowledgment log. It also recommends SharePoint content approval, so drafts stay hidden until someone signs off. Use the Word file for the text, and the log for who read and approved it.
Mistakes that lose the trail

items: Accepting all changes before you save a copy. Keep the tracked version as the record.
Leaving Track Changes on in the final file. Check the Review tab before you send.
Sending a file with comments still in it outside the team. Resolve or delete comments first.
Turning Track Changes off to tidy up. That removes the trail of who changed a clause.

blocks.text: Keep a version history that holds up later

Version history is where compliance records go wrong. The file name says final, but the content is older. Or someone saves over the approved file. Pick one naming rule, and use it on every file in the policy folder.

A simple pattern works well: policy name, status, and date. For example, anti-bribery-policy-final-YYYY-MM-DD.docx. Put the real date in place of the placeholder when you save. Sorting by name then keeps each policy's finals in date order.

Save each approved final in a separate folder that only the policy owner can edit. Run every Compare against that copy. The baseline then never drifts, and your redlines always start from what was actually approved.
Check your Word install before a policy deadline

This is the most urgent item on this page. Microsoft says that starting July 13, 2026, some Mac installs may enter a reduced functionality mode. This may apply to Microsoft 365 subscribers on macOS, and to non-subscription Office 2021 and Office 2019 on macOS. In that mode, Word can open and print files, but it cannot edit, save, or create new files.

If that happens in a deadline week, you cannot finish the redline. Check now. Open Word > About Word to see your version. Then ask your IT team whether your license puts you in scope. Do not wait for the first failed save.

For version context, Microsoft's release notes list Office for Mac version 16.114.3, dated Oct 27, 2026. The Word entry lists only quality and performance improvements. I found no 2026 Word feature change for Mac in those notes. Microsoft may update its known-issues page, so check it again before you rely on it.
Where Lazur fits in, and where it does not

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. Lazur sees the screen while you hold the shortcut, answers out loud, and draws a circle and label around the thing you ask about.

For how-to questions, Lazur guides you one click at a time and waits for each click. It does not click for you. It does not edit your files or operate other apps. It is not an add-in for Word, and Lazur has no partnership with any app maker.

Good uses on this job include asking where Compare Documents sits, asking what a strikethrough means, dictating clause text, and setting a reminder for the next review date. Apple Reminders and Calendar events are both on the list of things Lazur does by voice.

Background research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. Check every source before it goes into a policy. A summary is a starting point, not a citation.

Privacy matters for policy work. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Still, check your company's rules before you share internal documents with any AI tool.
There is a free trial with no credit card. Plans and prices are on the pricing page at /pricing, and the Mac app is at /download.
Dictate policy language without retyping it

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app, Word included. Use it to get a first draft of a clause onto the page fast. Then read every word, because exact wording carries weight in a policy.
Small word changes change the obligation. Must, should and may create different commitments. Speech is quick, so check modal verbs by hand before the text goes to a reviewer.

Use the personal dictionary for names your team uses, such as policy titles, committee names and regulator names. Snippets can hold a standard approval block or a standard scope statement. You can also check how your own speech comes out with the /tools/dictation-accuracy-checker.

blocks.title: Save a clean original
blocks.text: Save each approved final in a folder that only the policy owner can edit. Run every Compare against that copy, so the baseline never drifts.
Mistakes compliance officers make in Word on Mac

items: Comparing a draft to an email attachment, not the approved final. The redline then shows edits nobody approved.
Saving over the last final. Use a new file name for each approved version.
Editing in Word for the web, then expecting Compare to work there. It does not, because Compare and Merge is desktop only.
Treating the template as an approval system. Pair it with a separate acknowledgment log.
Checking the license state the week the policy is due.
Forgetting to update the table of contents after a section moves.

blocks.text: A setup checklist for your next policy cycle

items: Open Word > About Word and note your version.
Copy the policy template. Fill in the title page and version field.
Apply heading styles with ⌘⌥1 and insert the table of contents.
Agree on one file naming rule with your reviewers.
Turn on Track Changes with ⌘⇧E before the first review.
Run Compare Documents against the last approved final when the draft comes back.
Record the approval in your acknowledgment log, outside the Word file.

faq.question: Can I compare two Word documents on a Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the newer file in Word for Mac, then go to Review > Compare > Compare Documents. Select the original and the revised file and click OK. Word creates a new document with revision marks and leaves both source files unchanged. Microsoft's guide was written for Word 2019 for Mac, so menu labels may shift a little in newer versions.

faq.question: Does Word for the web have Compare Documents?
faq.answer: No. Microsoft's features comparison lists Compare and Merge revisions as a desktop-only feature. Track Changes appears in both the desktop and web versions. If a reviewer edits online, download the file and run Compare in Word for Mac.

faq.question: Why are my files grayed out in the Compare dialog?
faq.answer: Microsoft reports this after the update to Word for Mac version 16.109. Click Show Options in the file dialog, then change the file type from Templates to All Files. The Microsoft article was last updated May 18, 2026.

faq.question: Will my Word file stop working after July 13, 2026?
faq.answer: Not for everyone. Microsoft says a reduced functionality mode may affect Microsoft 365 subscribers on macOS, and non-subscription Office 2021 and Office 2019 on macOS. In that mode Word can open and print but cannot edit, save, or create files. Check Word > About Word, then ask your IT team.

faq.question: Is there a free Word template for policies?
faq.answer: Collaboris publishes a free policy and procedure template for Microsoft Word. It has a title page with a version number, a table of contents and nine sections. It has no acknowledgment section, so keep an acknowledgment log separately.

faq.question: How long should I keep superseded policy versions?
faq.answer: Collaboris cites the HIPAA Security Rule for keeping written policies for six years. That rule may not apply to your business. Check your regulator and your company's retention schedule before you set a period.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my policy in Word?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It can point at the Review tab, explain a revision mark out loud, and guide you one click at a time. It can also dictate text at your cursor while you hold fn.

faq.question: Does Lazur store the policy text I show it?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you and are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Check your company rules before you share internal documents with any AI tool.
